extracted.intended_audience: practitioners before the USPTO, disciplinary counsel, and OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: A final order implementing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24: it describes the procedural prerequisites (notice/service and opportunity to respond), the substantive misconduct relied upon, the scope of discipline, publication/notice obligations, and the practitioner's post-discipline duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline filed a 'Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' requesting that the Director of the USPTO impose reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by the Supreme Court of Ohio in Cincinnati Bar Association v. Rodger William Moore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure under § 11.24 permits the USPTO to impose reciprocal discipline based on discipline by a state authority. The process includes issuance of a Notice and Order, opportunity for the respondent to oppose on regulatory grounds, and entry of reciprocal discipline where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and service requirements (certified mail and delivery)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' was mailed by certified mail (receipt nos. listed) and was delivered to Respondent on January 20, 2016.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service (e.g., certified mail with receipts and proof of delivery) is required to trigger the statutory/regulatory response period and to support reciprocal discipline if the respondent fails to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond within forty (40) days
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the Supreme Court of Ohio, based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A timely response must assert one or more of the specific defenses listed in § 11.24(d)(1). Failure to timely file such a response forfeits those procedural protections and may lead to a default determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond (default/no genuine issue of material fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and suspension is the appropriate discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the respondent does not respond within the prescribed period, the USPTO may treat the state discipline as establishing the facts and impose reciprocal discipline without further factual dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) — types of misconduct relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Moore was found to have violated 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon being suspended by a state for: engaging in illegal acts that adversely reflected on his honesty and trustworthiness; engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, deceit, fraud or misrepresentation; engaging in illegal conduct involving moral turpitude; knowingly making false statements of material fact in connection with a disciplinary matter; and neglecting or refusing to participate in a disciplinary matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO will rely on the state authority's findings of misconduct (including specific categories such as dishonesty, moral turpitude, false statements, neglect of disciplinary proceedings) as the substantive basis for USPTO discipline under the referenced regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of discipline (areas of practice affected)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from the practice of trademark and non-patent law before the USPTO for one year, and is placed on probation for one year; Mr. Moore is not authorized to practice before the Office in patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal discipline may mirror the state-imposed sanction but is applied with respect to the practitioner’s USPTO-authorized practice areas (e.g., trademark/non-patent practice vs. patent practice). The order should specify the practice areas and any probationary conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication in Official Gazette and OED Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the following Notice in the Official Gazette (full Notice text provided). Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted for public reading at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (URL given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO publicly publishes notices of discipline (Official Gazette and OED Reading Room) including factual predicate and regulatory basis so the public and other agencies are informed of disciplinary actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO must notify relevant state disciplinary bodies and courts of the imposition and reasons for discipline to ensure interjurisdictional awareness and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplined practitioners are required to follow the specific post-discipline duties listed in § 11.58 (e.g., notice to clients and tribunals, surrendering of practice privileges where applicable); the order references compliance even though the duties are not reproduced in full in this document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of state adjudications as predicate evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court of Ohio's findings (e.g., seven incidents of shoplifting between 2001 and 2012 and submission of false statements during a disciplinary investigation) are cited as the factual basis for the USPTO's reciprocal action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final disciplinary findings by a duly constituted state authority serve as the factual predicate for USPTO reciprocal discipline; the USPTO relies on those findings rather than re-litigating the underlying misconduct when procedural prerequisites are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for discipline (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO disciplinary actions rest on statutory authority (35 U.S.C. § 32) and implementing regulations (§ 11.24); orders should cite these authorities when imposing discipline.
